rows.author: G118
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A REINVESTMENT FRAMEWORK FOR REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUST (REIT) SPONSORS, AMENDING SECTIONS 3, 8, AND 9 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9856, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS \"THE REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUST (REIT) ACT OF 2009\"
rows.title_short: Providing For A Reinvestment Framework For Real Estate Investment Trust (reit) Sponsors
rows.abstract:
Intends to ensure that the funds invested through the \"Real Estate Investment Act of 2009\" , enacted to promote the development of the capital market to fund infrastructure projects and further improve the real estate industry, are to be reinvested in the Philippines to secure full domestic participation in the real estate industry. Defines the terms \"REINVESTMENT PLAN\" and provides that any proceeds realized by the sponsor/promoter from the sale of R E I T share or other securities issued in exchange for income - generating real estate transferred to R E I T and any money raised by the sponsor/promoter from the sale of any of its income - generating to the R E I T, in any real estate including any redevelopment thereof, and/or infrastructure projects in the country, must be reinvested in the Philippines.

Mandates that the REIT shall submit a Reinvestment Plan to the Exchange or the Commission upon registration and must annually secure a Certification from the Commission that it is compliant with its Reinvestment Plan.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2020-06-01, transmitted to the Senate on 2020-06-03 and received by the Senate on 2020-06-03

rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING A MORATORIUM ON THE OPEN PIT METHOD OF MINING FOR COPPER, GOLD, SILVER, AND COMPLEX ORES IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: “ Open Pit Mining Moratorium Act ”
rows.abstract:
Provides for a 25-year moratorium or suspension on the approval and commencement of mining projects which covers all existing approved and pending mining projects that have not commenced commercial operation.
Intends to craft a National Industrialization Program (NIP) and a Mineral Management Plan (MMP) as a precondition to the consideration of the feasibility of open-pit mining method after a mandatory review of this Act after twelve (12) years.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2020-03-09

rows.author: D055
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING PUBLIC SOLICITATIONS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.title_short: “ Public Solicitations Act.”
rows.abstract:
Intends to regulate public solicitation by any organizations, agencies, groups and individuals in order to protect the general public from unscrupulous solicitation and to ensure that funds are properly utilized for the intended charitable, social or public welfare purposes and for the intended beneficiaries.

Provides for the following, among others: 1. All agencies and organizations covered and exempted by this Act; 2. Documentary requirements for solicitation permit; 3. Officials who are authorized to issue permit ; 4. The validity of permit; 5. Types of public solicitation; 6. Fees and charges; 7. Methods of public solicitation; 8. Allocation of proceeds; 9. Monitoring of public solicitation; 10. Reportorial requirements for exempt organizations; and 11. Prohibited acts and penalties

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL HEALTH SECURITY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short:
Aims To Establish The Systems And Engagement Needed To Detect And Control Potential Disease Outbreaks Like The On-going Surge In Novel Coronavirus (covid-19), By Developing A National Sop/equivalent That Describes The Coordination And Communication Among The Multiple Agencies In The Implementation Of The International Health Regulation (ihr} And Strengthen The Strategic Health Emergency Risk Assessments Using Multiple Sources Of Information, With Focus On Health Risk, Health Impacts And The Vulnerability Of Health System.
Intends To Address The Fact That Only Few Countries Have The Capacities Required Under The Ihr); That Great Majority Of National Health Systems Would Be Unable To Handle A Large Influx Of Patients Infected With A Respiratory Pathogen Capable Of Easy Transmissibility And High Mortality; And That The Joint External Evaluation (jee) Of Ihr Core Capacities Of The Country Reveals That There Are Still Challenges In Achieving Harmonized Approach For Ihr Implementation, Among Others.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE NATIONAL PROGRAM FOR THE ELIMINATION OF TUBERCULOSIS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10767 OR THE \"COMPREHENSIVE TUBERCULOSIS ELIMINATION PLAN ACT\"
rows.title_short: Strengthening The National Program For The Elimination Of Tuberculosis,
rows.abstract:
Seeks to support and expand efforts to eliminate tuberculosis as a public health problem in the country by intensifying information and education programs on the principles and practices of preventing, detecting, managing and controlling tuberculosis, as well as development and inclusion of curricula about tuberculosis in the basic education.

Provides for the following significant features, among others: provisions on patients´ rights and responsibilities, corporate social responsibility to encourage business corporations to contribute in the on-going efforts to reduce the incidence of TB in the country; convergence of services; TB Strategic Plan for local government units; integration of TB services into established Service Delivery Networks (SDNs) or local health referral system; and inclusion of TB-DOTS treatment as one of the requirements for the conditional cash transfer program.
